liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (5 reviews): Reviewer says Jerry's solo ends in a clumsy return to the verse; the following jam is decent but unremarkable; Healy's mixing handles Bobby's emotional outburst in the coda well, per the reviewer [15][18][22][24][26]
- **Eyes of the World** (5 reviews): Reviewer calls this one of the fastest Eyes of the World of the era, or of nearly any era; Estimated leads into a very fast, supercharged Eyes that the reviewer now rates a personal favorite [18][19][22][24][26]
- **Throwing Stones** (2 reviews): Bobby wails on Throwing Stones, per the reviewer; Jerry's lead at the end of Throwing Stones is called phenomenal [19][25]
- **The Wheel** (2 reviews): The new-age style jam after Drums leading into The Wheel is described as serene; Space leads into a Wheel the reviewer finds unbelievable, followed by China Doll [23][25]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Jerry and the drummers lose the beat at the opening, according to the reviewer [15]
- **Desolation Row** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the best Desolation Row ever [19]
- **Hell in a Bucket** (1 review): Hell in a Bucket starts well and grows great, though Bob gets goofy with the delay effect [22]
- **Turn on Your Lovelight** (1 review): Reviewer laughs at Bob outdoing himself on Lovelight [25]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd86-05-10 01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd86-05-10 02 Bertha**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd86-05-10 03 Greatest Story Ever Told**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd86-05-10 04 West LA Fadeaway**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd86-05-10 05 Desolation Row**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd86-05-10 06 Tennessee Jed**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd86-05-10 07 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **gd86-05-10 08 Big Railroad Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1986-05-10.140256.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 22 songs; 166 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd86-05-10.sbd.hinko.19962.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 164 min; rated 4.33/5 by 21 [2]
- **gd1986-05-10.176988.matrix.shubert.flac2444**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 166 min [4]
- **gd1986-05-10.166966.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 164 min [6]
- **gd1986-05-10.156609.nakomni.holbrook.flac24**: source not stated; 20 songs; 162 min [10]

## Around the show

- Tapers had been told the previous weekend not to record front-of-board at the Frost [10]
- Reviewer likens the chills from Bobby's Estimated fanfare to Jerry's fanfare in Fire on the Mountain, Omni 3.27.89 [18]
- Reviewer ranks this Wheel as possibly second best, after the Long Beach 1981 version [23]
- Bobby raves throughout Estimated, as he does in the Red Rocks 85 version, per the reviewer [23]
- Reviewer likens the chills from Bobby's Estimated fanfare to Jerry's fanfare in Fire on the Mountain, Omni 3.27.89 [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1986-05-10.140256.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk41.oade.wise.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Charlie Miller, Jim Wise, Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: (FOB) Schoeps CMC4/MK41 (120 degree ORTF)> Oade M118 > Sony PCM-F1; Transfer Info: Master Oade PCM (unknown deck/hardware/software) > hard disk >… [1]. Also: Source uses Schoeps microphones, recorded front-of-board, per the file name; Jim Wise supplied the drive and Charlie Miller coordinated [1]
- **gd86-05-10.sbd.hinko.19962.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [2]. Also: Reviewer bought this show on cassette for 8.95 at the Now and Then Shop, a hippie store in New Hope, PA [17]
- **gd1986-05-10.176988.matrix.shubert.flac2444**: source: SBD/AUD Matrix Blend by Ryan Schubert [4]. Also: Matrix mix of soundboard and audience sources, about 60/40 soundboard-dominant, with sub-bass entirely from the soundboard; Mixed in Reaper at 24-bit/44.1 kHz with light EQ in iZotope Ozone; sources loudness-matched and sample-aligned per song [4]
- **gd1986-05-10.166966.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5 [6]. Also: A Nakamichi 700 source from Bob Wagner patches an eight-second gap in Drums [6]
- **gd1986-05-10.156609.nakomni.holbrook.flac24**: taped by Executive Crew, Mike Davis, Kenny Davis, Aaron; patched out of Poris/Olness custom rig; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: 1GEN AUDCA Microphones: Jaime Poris custom mics: Nakamichi capsules customized, attached to plexiglass plates spread 20 feet apart > dbx 224|customized > Dolby… [10]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Frost Amphitheatre - May 10, 1986](https://www.dead.net/show/may-10-1986) [28]
- Poster by Wolfgang's: [Grateful Dead Laminate from Frost Amphitheatre, May 10, 1986 at Wolfgang's](https://www.wolfgangs.com/backstage-passes/grateful-dead/laminate/FRA860510.html) [29]
